title: Emergency capacity triage and policy guardrails for Dedicated Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures emergency triage steps, short-to-long term guardrails, and action items after a capacity shortfall and autoscaler regression that reduced effective throughput across multiple Dedicated pools for ~45 minutes. The goal is to preserve SLAs for premium customers, stopgap mitigations for ongoing traffic, and a prioritized roadmap to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-04 19:12 UTC we observed a simultaneous increase in queue_wait_ms and drop in tokens/sec for two Dedicated GPU pools in us-west-2. Autoscaler recommendations were suppressed due to a regression in the scale decision scorer introduced in runtime-1.18. Downscales happened aggressively (scale_down_cooldown mis-configured), causing headroom to evaporate and triggering throttles for best-effort tenants. Impact lasted ~45 minutes; SLOs for P1 customers were degraded but no data exfiltration or security event occurred.
timeline: 2026-03-04 19:12 UTC — page issued: capacity_alert for pool:dedicated-us-west-2-gpu-pool-A (queue_wait_ms > 2500ms)
2026-03-04 19:16 UTC — oncall runbook started by Aisha Patel; initial mitigation: raised per-route emergency throttle for non-VIP customers via console route-profile
2026-03-04 19:22 UTC — autoscaler logs reviewed: scale decision scorer returned negative weight for pending queue due to new decay factor in runtime-1.18 (PR #3124)
2026-03-04 19:28 UTC — manual scale-up executed: added 4 nodes to pool-A (temporary burst capacity), kernel warm-up observed after ~90s
2026-03-04 19:55 UTC — traffic stabilized; queue_wait_ms returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated. Post-incident collection initiated.
2026-03-05 09:00 UTC — initial postmortem draft and RCA hypothesis shared with SRE/Runtime/PM teams (contribs: SRE: Marco Rivera, Runtime: Leila Gomez)
2026-03-06 14:35 UTC — runbook and alert thresholds amended to add multi-metric escalation (queue_wait_ms + effective_headroom_pct)
2026-03-08 11:00 UTC — this ticket created to track guardrails, fixes, and rollout plan
mitigations_taken: Raised per-route emergency throttles for non-VIP customers to preserve headroom for reserved tenants
Manual burst addition of 4 nodes to affected pool to restore throughput
Rolled back the runtime-1.18 scorer change in canary pools and staged a hotfix to remove decay factor (PR #3189)
Added a temporary automation job that proactively warms KV caches and kernels on newly provisioned nodes (capacity-smoke)
root_cause_hypothesis: A recent change to the autoscaler scoring function (runtime-1.18 PR #3124) introduced an overly aggressive decay term for queued requests, which under certain queue patterns suppressed scale-up recommendations. Combined with an unintentionally long scale_down_cooldown value (600s) and missing multi-metric escalation in alerts, the system allowed headroom to drop below safe thresholds before automated mitigation could take place.
postmortem_actions: P0 (owner: Marco Rivera) — Emergency rollback permanently revert decay term and add a safety clamp on scorer outputs. Deliverable: runtime PR #3189 merged and canaried by 2026-03-09

P0 (owner: Leila Gomez) — Shorten scale_down_cooldown from 600s to 180s for all Dedicated pools and add per-pool min_nodes and min_headroom_pct (20% for VIP tiers). Rollout: staged via infra config; measure impact over 2 cycles

P1 (owner: Sanjay Kulkarni) — Add a composite alert: fire when queue_wait_ms > 1500ms AND effective_headroom_pct < 25% OR tokens/sec drops > 30% for 2 consecutive 1m windows. Update runbook to surface automated recommended play (manual scale or emergency throttle)
P1 (owner: Priya Nair) — Instrument new metric: autoscaler_suppression_reason and expose top-k reasons in Console for troubleshooting
P1 (owner: Rui Chen) — Implement conservative autoscaler fallback: if scorer returns suppression > 0.25, route decision to legacy heuristic until canary verification completes
P2 (owner: Designated) — Add reserved headroom config per-customer profile; default reserve 10% for standard, 20% for premium. UI + API change tracked in PM-1123
P2 (owner: SRE team) — Develop capacity-smoke runner as a managed job to keep a minimal warm kernel footprint and verify node readiness within 60s of spin-up
P2 (owner: Observability) — Build Grafana dashboard: "pool-headroom-dashboard" that shows headroom_pct, queue_wait_ms, tokens/sec, autoscaler_recommendation_score across pools (ref: GRAF-4207)
P3 (owner: Security) — Review any privilege implications of emergency throttle UI changes (note: no immediate security risk identified)
P3 (owner: Product) — Communicate incident summary and mitigation to impacted customers; offer credits where SLAs were violated
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix to scorer validated in canaries and promoted: no suppression anomalies for synthetic workloads (capacity-smoke) and real traffic within 48h
Scale_down_cooldown and min_headroom_pct config rolled out and verified in metrics for 2 production cycles
Composite alert deployed and exercised via tabletop drill; runbook updated with explicit manual steps
Console shows autoscaler_suppression_reason in route-level troubleshooting panel
Postmortem published and reviewed in Eng All-Hands; follow-up tickets created and prioritized
decisions: Rollback scorer decay term in runtime-1.18 rather than attempt blind parameter tuning in production
Favor conservative downscale defaults and explicit min_headroom_pct over aggressive auto-squeeze optimizations
Introduce a scorer fallback to legacy heuristic when suppression confidence is high
Prioritize observability for autoscaler decisions — reasons must be surfaced to operators
updates: 2026-03-06 — Short-term fixes implemented and canaried. Observability gaps identified: autoscaler suppression reasons and multi-metric alerts
2026-03-07 — Added capacity-smoke runner to staging; initial warm-up success for 3 node types
2026-03-08 — Drafted rollout plan for cooldown and headroom config; engineering review scheduled for 2026-03-09
